To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) mTOR regulates translation through multiple mechanisms; 2) mTOR regulates ribosome biogenesis; 3) mTOR regulates mRNA stability; 4) mTOR regulates the expression and activity of translation factors; 5) mTOR controls mRNA localization and translation; 6) mTOR controls the expression of translation initiation factors and the activity of translation initiation factors; 7) mTOR regulates RNA polymerase I and RNA polymerase II activity.
the mTOR pathway controls protein synthesis by regulating the expression of ribosomes and the biogenesis and activity of translation initiation factors.
mTOR is the central hub of the protein synthesis machinery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation and function of mTOR and its effectors in the control of cell growth.
the regulation of protein synthesis in eukaryotic cells, and how this process is controlled by mTOR.
the role of mTOR signaling in protein synthesis, cell growth and cell proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mTOR regulates protein synthesis by controlling the synthesis of the components required for protein synthesis.
mTOR is the master regulator of protein synthesis.
the mTOR pathway plays a central role in the control of cell growth and proliferation, and that the mTORC1 complex is a key regulator of protein synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mTOR is a central controller of protein synthesis in mammalian cells.
mTOR is a key regulator of protein synthesis.
we are interested in understanding the mechanisms that control the initiation and elongation of protein synthesis in mammalian cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mTOR is a master regulator of the protein synthetic machinery and that it is a major determinant of the translational capacity of the cell.
mTOR is a master regulator of protein synthesis, and that it controls protein synthesis at the level of the initiation and elongation steps.
the mTOR complex 2 (mTORC2)-mediated phosphorylation of S6K1 is essential for the activation of the protein synthesis machinery.
